pass_a_gloss: Print heading in Latin naming the theme: the synagogue’s downfall, that is, Abram’s change of name into Abraham. Greek lemma ascribing the excerpt to Saint Cyril and giving his treatise title: a proof built from heaven-sent sayings addressed to the patriarchs of old, about Jews and Gentiles trading places. Main claim: Abraham’s new name turns out to encode God’s threefold personal being, since heaven itself replaced the patriarch’s earlier name Abram with Abraham. Opening move of the letter proof: a reader who wishes to decode the name should combine its initial alpha with the beta stuck to it and shift across the alpha positioned past rho.
pass_b_english: On the falling away of the synagogue, or the renaming of Abram as Abraham.

Of Saint Cyril, from the discourse entitled Demonstration, through the divine oracles spoken from the first to the inspired patriarchs, concerning the exchange and transfer involving the Jews and the nations.
The renaming of Abraham has been found to signify the threefold count of the divine and sovereign persons: for though the inspired patriarch was called Abram, God renamed him Abraham (Genesis 17:5).

If anyone should choose to interpret the matter — taking the opening letter of the name, alpha, together with the letter joined and clinging to it, I mean beta — he will surely discover, by carrying over the alpha that stands after rho,

lemmas.gloss: renaming, new name in place of old

choices.choice: Inline citation beside the renaming clause; the event is narrated, not quoted.
Divine and sovereign persons: the adjective joins God’s being with his rule.
Open ends without a terminal period; the clause completes in frag-rem-early.
